title: Operator docs contradict reality: design-pack command still says built-in skills never install
description:
From the 2026-08-02 deep review (HIGH in pass 2, LOW in pass 1 — the severity disagreement is itself recorded; treat as HIGH because it is consumer-facing and actively misleads an autonomous agent).

**The defect.** TASK-181 changed what `reconcile-apply` actually does for a consumer, and touched NO file under `commands/`. The shipped operator-facing doc now describes the opposite of reality.

`commands/design-pack.md` still states that on a fresh project the expected first run is `installed: []`, with `ui-ux-pro-max` appearing under "skills that still need adoption" and its assimilate instruction shown. It further instructs: *"treat `installed` being short of the desired skill set as expected, not a bug, whenever a matching `skill:` entry exists in `packs[].report`."*

Post-TASK-181 a fresh consumer installs BOTH `skill:watch` and `skill:ui-ux-pro-max` from the plugin's owned copies (locked by `tests/e2e/pack-ctl-consumer-source.spec.js`). Consequences:

1. An orchestrator following Step 5 will tell a human to run `assimilate-current-project` for a skill that was already materialized.
2. Worse, it will read a genuine total failure as "expected" — re-creating precisely the blindness TASK-181 existed to remove.
3. Per the empty-box defect (TASK-183), a short `installed` can occur with NO matching `skill:` report entry at all, so the documented triage rule cannot detect that case even in principle.

Step 4's documented output shape is also stale: it says reconcile-apply "Prints `{ plan, packs: [{ id, owner, aborted, installed, report }] }`" with no mention of `ok`, `planned_install_count`, `installed_count`, or `source_root`. A grep for those field names across all `*.md` returns zero hits — they are documented nowhere in the repo.

**Second, independent item folded in (disjoint file, same class of drift).** `src/graph-freshness.js:61` now folds a malformed done-ticket key into the `missing` bucket (TASK-175 item 13). The live sensor message at `tests/graph-freshness.spec.js:155-159` still reports every entry uniformly as "have no `task-<digits>` node in knowledge/graph/graph.json" and advises "Run the backfill (or add the node via src/knowledge-graph.js addNode)". For a malformed key BOTH statements are wrong: no node id is derivable, and `scripts/backfill-graph-task-nodes.mjs:60-70` now deliberately THROWS on exactly that case. The detection changed; the remediation instruction did not.

**Scope note:** docs and one sensor message. This ticket must NOT change reconcile behavior — the behavioral fixes live in TASK-183. If writing the doc reveals that the behavior itself is wrong, raise it rather than fixing it here.
acceptance_criteria: commands/design-pack.md Step 4 documents reconcile-apply's ACTUAL output shape, including the ok, planned_install_count, installed_count and source_root fields, and states what ok:false means for the operator.

The 'treat a short installed as expected, not a bug' triage instruction is corrected so an agent following it can distinguish 'nothing needed installing' from 'something failed to install'. The fresh-project expectation (Steps 5 and the Notes bullet) is rewritten to match post-TASK-181 reality: built-in pack skills DO install from the plugin's owned copies.

A doc-lock spec pins the correspondence so this cannot silently drift again — e.g. asserting that the field names the CLI actually emits from reconcile-apply all appear in commands/design-pack.md. The spec must fail if a new top-level output field is added without documenting it (prove it fails by mutation).

The graph-freshness sensor message distinguishes the two cases it now detects: a done ticket with a derivable key but no graph node (backfill is the correct remedy) versus a done ticket with a malformed key (the backfill THROWS — the key must be fixed first). The advice given matches what the referenced script actually does.
No behavioral change to reconcile/apply logic in this ticket — verify with git diff that only docs, the sensor message, and their specs changed. Behavioral fixes belong to TASK-183.
npm test (fast tier) and npm run test:all are green; no existing spec regresses.

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body:
CLOSED on a green re-review after one RC loop. **APPROVE — 0 HIGH / 0 MEDIUM / 3 LOW.** All 6 ACs PASS.

**Review depth: `full`** on both passes — rubric inputs for the fix round: 210 changed lines (>=150) and the diff modifies a sensor spec (test infrastructure).

## RC loop history (one round)
First attempt `ff1d07b` returned REQUEST-CHANGES with 2 HIGH. Both are now verified CLOSED by the reviewer's own external mutation runs, not by taking the developer's word:

**HIGH-1 (doc stale at HEAD) — CLOSED.** The doc was accurate when written, then sibling ticket TASK-183 (`0a76ae2`) landed two minutes later and changed the behavior underneath it. Fix round `e6a9810` re-synced Step 4 against HEAD field-for-field: `ok:true` is now the only success path (requiring `installed_count === planned_install_count` AND no abort), all three failure kinds are named with correct predicates and abort precedence, all three `E_PACK_APPLY_*` code values are enumerated verbatim, and the exit-1 + message-on-stderr contract is documented. Crucially the fix caught DOWNSTREAM surfaces too, not just the paragraph it was pointed at — Step 4's triage bullet, Step 5's tail note, the fresh-project paragraph, and the Notes bullet. A whole-file grep for surviving "short/zero installed is expected" claims returns none.

**HIGH-2 (vacuous doc-lock) — CLOSED.** Both structural blind spots closed and mutation-proven externally: (1) a failure-path fixture forcing `ok:false` via `HIVEMIND_OWNED_SOURCE_ROOT` so failure-only fields actually enter the checked set; (2) a word-boundary predicate replacing `doc.includes(field)`. The decisive proof: with every standalone word `code` stripped from the doc but "hardcoded"/"hardcode" left intact, the failure-path lock FAILS — simultaneously demonstrating the substring coincidence no longer fools it AND that the new fixture is what carries the failure-only fields.

## LOW-1 — the residual worth carrying forward (read this before the next pack-ctl change)
The reviewer pushed past the ACs and found the boundary of what this lock can do: **it pins field-NAME presence anywhere in the file, not Step-4 locality and not semantics.** Mutation 3 showed that adding the word "code" in an unrelated appended sentence makes the lock pass again, and by construction a field whose name is documented but whose MEANING is wrong — which is precisely the HIGH-1 drift mode — still passes.

Assessed as an acceptable residual against AC3's own letter (which specifies a name-presence lock), and both historical drifts did involve UNDOCUMENTED NEW fields, which this lock now catches on both output paths. But a pure semantics-only drift (e.g. `ok`'s meaning changing again with no field change) remains **process-covered only**. Cheap hardening the reviewer identified for whoever next touches this surface: the doc enumerates the three `E_PACK_APPLY_*_FAILURE` values, but the spec only locks the word `code` — asserting the actual `result.code` VALUE from the failure run appears in the doc would pin one semantic edge for free.

## Other LOWs (non-blocking)
Test (b) of the predicate-hardening block exercises an inline reimplementation of the OLD substring predicate — dead code that cannot catch a live regression, since a revert of `assertFieldsDocumented` is already caught by test (a). Documentation value only; redundant under the new-test budget. And `source_root` is described as "the directory the reconciler vendored owned skill copies from" when it is really the resolved FALLBACK root appended to the search path — `applyPlan` always leads with `<repoRoot>/assimilated-skills`, so a self-assimilated skill vendors from the project root even when `source_root` names the plugin's dir. The null-vs-non-null triage the doc emphasizes is unaffected.

## Gate
`test:since -- 180fa3d` 10 files / 99 passed (non-empty selection) · `npm test` 77 files / 1043 passed, 2 skipped · `design-pack-doc-lock.spec.js` 5/5 · `npm run test:all` 171 files / 1969 passed, 4 skipped — identical to the `fb2692d` baseline the Orchestrator independently verified on a clean tree · `graph-freshness.spec.js` 11/11 including the 3 AC4 tests · `check:calibration` no violations.

## AC4 and AC5 preserved from the first attempt
The graph-freshness message split (`buildMissingMessage`) was untouched by the fix round and its three tests still pass; `scripts/backfill-graph-task-nodes.mjs` really does throw on the malformed-key case the message claims. `git diff 180fa3d e6a9810 --stat` confirms exactly 2 files, no `src/`/`bin/`/`dist/`.

## Concurrency hygiene — the mitigation worked
`e6a9810` was committed while TASK-185 had uncommitted work in the same tree, using a pathspec-limited `git commit -- <paths>` instead of `git add` + `git commit`. `git show --name-only` lists exactly the 2 intended files with no sibling contamination — in contrast to the first attempt, which produced an 11-file commit and had to be reset. The hazard and the mitigation are tracked in TASK-191.

## Provenance
This ticket's defect was found by the 2026-08-02 two-pass adversarial deep review (HIGH in one pass, LOW in the other — the severity disagreement is recorded in the ticket description). Its own fix then went stale within two minutes because a sibling ticket changed the documented behavior, which is itself the clearest available evidence for why doc-vs-code correspondence needs a mechanical lock rather than a convention.
